messages:
Maya (support): Customer escalation - p95/p99 generation latency spiked after our maintenance window. They've attached traces and a minimal repro harness.
Ibrahim - eng-sre: Region/pool and hardware? Any immediate customer impact?
Maya (support): ap-southeast-2, dedicated pool dpool-asia-7, H100 hosts with local Intel P5510 NVMe. Their p99 jumped from ~140ms -> ~1.6s during the maintenance window; production traffic affected.
Claire (infra): We rolled kernel 6.4.7 and updated the nvidia driver package to 567.03 Saturday night. No NVMe firmware changes. Collecting dmesg, /proc/interrupts and nvme-cli outputs from affected nodes.
Rohit (storage): NVMe SMART clean, but iostat shows occasional svctm spikes up to 300-450ms on nvme0n1 concurrent with the API tails. fio run from their harness attached shows heavy tail at p99.
Zoe (runtime): Traces show stalls in token emission and blocking in the runtime waiting on page-ins; strace shows long `io_getevents` and `io_submit` blocking. KV cache hit rate steady so this looks like storage-tail.
Ibrahim - eng-sre: Can we test quick sysfs changes on one repro host: `cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` and `cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/rq_affinity` and try `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` + `echo 2 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/rq_affinity`? Also check `cat /proc/interrupts | grep nvme`.
Claire (infra): On the repro host scheduler is `kyber [mq-deadline] none` (kyber active) and rq_affinity=1. NVMe MSI-X pinned to cpus 8-11. I'll flip to mq-deadline and set rq_affinity=2 on one canary now.
Maya (support): Customer repro steps: single-threaded generator, seq len ~1024, concurrency 4. They provided an fio command: `fio --name=randrw --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randrw --bs=64k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=4 --time_based --runtime=60` and `iostat -xz 1` output.
Rohit (storage): After switching scheduler + rq_affinity on the canary, a synthetic run dropped p99 from ~1.6s -> ~420ms. That's a strong signal.
Zoe (runtime): Runtime side mitigations: immediate route to spare dedicated pool dpool-asia-spare-1 and enable per-route concurrency cap (3). Also enable experimental async weight prefetch for this customer's model so page-ins are less blocking.
Ibrahim - eng-sre: I'll change routing and push a temporary control-plane throttle. Meanwhile capture `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` on the tuned host during a repro and bpftrace for `io_getevents` and `block:block_rq_complete` events.
Claire (infra): Routing applied to spare pool. Observability shows p99 returned to baseline there. On the original pool I'm also going to try restarting irqbalance and observing if IRQs rebalance the NVMe vectors.
Rohit (storage): Additional experiment: I lowered the NVMe controller submission queue depth on a test host using `nvme set-feature --feature-id=0x7 --value=32` and saw reduced tail variance but decreased max throughput. Could be an acceptable trade for latency-sensitive tenants.
Zoe (runtime): Also add a short-lived circuit breaker in runtime: when host.iowait > 25% or nvme_p99 > 150ms, drop new requests to that host and route existing ones away. This should prevent cascading tails.
Maya (support): Customer confirmed better latency on the spare pool. They're asking for RCA and ETA on a permanent fix; also asked about SLA credits. I've looped Asha from accounts.
Asha (acct): Noted. We'll wait for RCA before discussing credits. Keep me updated.
Claire (infra): Action plan: 1) Canary rollback one host to previous kernel image (6.3.x) tomorrow morning to see if that reproduces baseline; 2) if rollback is not feasible across fleet, push safe sysfs tuning (mq-deadline, rq_affinity=2, reduce vm.dirty_ratio) as an interim; 3) gather perf/bpf traces and open vendor ticket if driver/kernel interaction suspected.
Rohit (storage): I'll run a fio matrix (iodepth 8/16/32/64) across kernel/driver permutations and capture `perf script` and SPDK traces where available. Also will collect NVMe SMART deltas.
Ibrahim - eng-sre: I'll assemble a vendor packet with `perf`/bpf traces and top-of-stack block layer callstacks. If we see `blk_mq_wait_for_request`/`nvme_submit_async_event` patterns we'll escalate to the driver/kernel maintainers.
Zoe (runtime): Runtime follow-ups: 1) enable async prefetch for models on NVM-backed pools; 2) lower default batch sizes for sensitive routes; 3) add syscall-level trace when `io_submit/io_getevents` exceed 50ms to capture stacks.
Maya (support): Created internal incident ticket INC-8231 and uploaded customer repro and fio outputs. Customer wants hourly updates until RCA.
incident-bot: Incident owners assigned -> Claire (infra), Rohit (storage), Ibrahim - eng-sre
Claire (infra): I'll post perf artifacts in the ticket once capture completes. Next update in 2 hours.
Ibrahim - eng-sre: Keeping the incident open until canary rollback or kernel-driver bisect completes.
Maya (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
